signals.name: Pieter Abbeel
signals.text:
Game changer for humanoid full-body control training.  Now it's superfast (and cheap, just one GPU) to train a single policy on *all* the motions.  How come:
(1) World model much faster than regular sim
(2) Backprop through time collects way more signal than policy gradients

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
We hope FairStress gives researchers a way to uncover hidden asymmetries in model decision-making, test fixes, & develop more consistent systems.
📝 Blog: allenai.org/blog/fairstress
📄 Paper: allenai.org/papers/fairstr…

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text: Since LLMs have various biases in their decisions and reasoning, we then examined how training data might influence this, & find that LLMs are never really taught fair decision-making yet are often aligned to prevent discrimination—which may explain over-correction patterns.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
We tested 9 approaches for reducing these gaps. Most didn’t reliably improve symmetric robustness; some hurt performance.
Older benchmarks like BBQ can miss overcorrection, but FairStress reveals the hidden asymmetries they overlook.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
Next, we want HiRO-ACEv2 to work across more climates—not just the one it was trained on.
We’re training it on observed-weather & +4°C datasets, adding outputs like temperature, snow, & ice + exploring ways to make HiROv2 10×+ faster.
Read more: buff.ly/NAfRlQI

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
Together, ACE + HiROv2 can generate years of global climate data at resolutions fine enough to capture storms, severe winds, & other local extreme events.
And it’s cheap: global 3 km simulations cost ~300× less than X-SHiELD, with even bigger savings for individual regions.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
HiROv2 is especially strong on extremes: it matches the distribution of extreme events in X-SHiELD to within 3% for 1-in-a-million rain, wind, & pressure predictions.
It also captures cyclone energy, realistic hurricanes, & strong downslope winds.
Demo: ace.allen.ai

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text: Molmo 2 already knew how to track objects in video. Its open code let Kai modify the model, while its open training data helped him understand what it had learned and prepare his own data—turning a general-purpose model into one tailored to his research.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
Kai fine-tuned Molmo 2 on sonar video then trained it on examples of tracking errors, instructions, & corrections.
In tests, Molmo2Fish could fix some mistakes after guidance—for example, when two salmon had been assigned the same track.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
Tracking salmon by analyzing video helps researchers monitor their populations. But when a salmon-tracking system makes a mistake, like an overcount, fixing it can mean editing clips frame after frame by hand.
What if you could just tell the system to fix what it got wrong?

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text: Compare responses from models & human tutors in the new explorer experience, where you can also examine model tutoring performance alongside response time and cost: tutormoments.allen.ai

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
When asked to “tutor well,” Claude Sonnet 5.5 (low effort) was best at asking students to work through more of a math problem themselves when teachers recommended it.
With explicit tutoring instructions, GPT-6 Sol (no reasoning) outscored Claude Opus 4.8 overall.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
In these tests, GPT-6 models over-help less than earlier OpenAI models.
They also score higher overall when we explicitly instruct them to offer help where needed while leaving students to work through parts of a problem they can handle themselves.
